assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data turned intergenerational mobility into a measurable, place-specific quantity. The work combines careful measurement with credible causal designs (movers, Moving to Opportunity re-analysis) and has had large effects on how economists and policymakers study opportunity. Measurement and causal inference are done together, which I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure. Hendren is a principal co-author of the exposure-effects and place-based causal work. Katz is a senior contributor through Moving to Opportunity and long-run neighbourhood effects. Friedman and others are also important, so the three-name limit forces a difficult cut.
assessment.maturity: The core mobility papers date from 2014 onward, and the causal place-effects work is still being replicated and extended. The agenda is influential but young by Nobel standards, so some caution about timing is warranted.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat this as one discovery or as a series of data-driven empirical contributions.
Robustness of the place-effect estimates and the stability of the findings over time.
Difficult attribution among Chetty, Hendren, Friedman and Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint mechanism of Kiyotaki and Moore gives a rigorous account of how credit frictions amplify and propagate shocks. It is foundational for modern macro-finance and crisis analysis, and it is still taught and used widely, including in policy models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle model. Gertler is credited here for the financial-accelerator and macro-financial integration line. Bernanke, who shared the 2022 prize, and Gilchrist are also linked to the financial accelerator, so the Gertler credit is less clean than the other two.
assessment.maturity: The central papers are from 1997 and have decades of confirmation and extension, including after 2008. It is a mature contribution.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
Whether Gertler's inclusion is better than a two-person award.
Direct empirical identification of the collateral channel is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model and its extension to decentralised markets are foundational game theory. They gave a tractable strategic basis for bargaining and price formation and underpin much work in labour, search, finance and industrial organisation.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the originator of the alternating-offers solution. Wolinsky is the co-author of the market-bargaining synthesis. Binmore made important related contributions on the Nash program and bargaining, but his attribution is secondary to the core results.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The results are more than 40 years old, canonical and uncontested. Any timing concern is about prior non-recognition, not about doubt over validity.
uncertainties: Binmore's relative credit and the Nash-program lineage, including Stahl and Ståhl-type precursors.
Whether the committee prefers recent empirical or applied work over foundational theory this year.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz (2003) model of firm heterogeneity and selection changed international trade by explaining within-industry reallocation and a new channel for welfare gains. It is the main framework for modern empirical and quantitative trade work, and it links micro firm data to aggregate outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the originator of the heterogeneous-firm model. Helpman contributed through the Helpman–Melitz–Yeaple extension on exporting versus FDI and through earlier work on trade and increasing returns. Redding is an important later contributor, but I weigh him as secondary.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of extensive empirical confirmation and extension. It is mature enough for consideration.
uncertainties: Krugman's 2008 prize already recognised the monopolistic-competition foundation of the new trade theory.
Possible overlap with B013 and B042 in the trade field.
Attribution relative to Bernard–Jensen firm-level empirical findings, who are not named here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock studies and the task-based analysis of labour demand gave credible, locally identified evidence on how trade and technology reshape employment, wages and politics. This is an influential policy-relevant empirical contribution with real causal-inference quality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the three principal authors of the China-shock papers. Autor also has distinct earlier task-framework work with Levy and Murnane. Katz is credited in the longlist for earlier skill-biased change work but is excluded here to keep the group coherent.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock work is from about 2013 onward. It has been replicated and debated, with some disputes about magnitude. It is reasonably mature but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 and 2019 prizes on technology and empirical development economics.
Ongoing debate on the size and persistence of the effects and on identification choices.
Whether the task-based line belongs more to Autor alone and to Acemoglu, who was already recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Building long-run top-income and wealth series from tax and national-accounts data transformed the measurement of inequality and shaped the debate worldwide. As historical data infrastructure it is a major scholarly contribution, even though the theoretical interpretation is more contested.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the founders of the top-income series. Zucman is the leader on offshore wealth and distributional national accounts. The three are tightly linked in the data programme, but the interpretive claims in Piketty's book are separate from the measurement contribution.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from the early 2000s and has been widely replicated. The wealth, offshore and distributional accounts are still developing and are debated methodologically.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over wealth capitalisation and the trends in recent decades.
Whether the committee values the data and measurement contribution as much as a theoretical or identification advance.
Policy and political visibility of the authors could affect committee perception.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework offers a disciplined quantitative way to explain cross-country productivity gaps through the distribution of resources across firms and sectors. It connects micro-data to aggregate income differences and has shaped development and growth research.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the central authors. Restuccia and Rogerson are the other main originators of the misallocation approach, and Restuccia is credited here for the agricultural and aggregate versions. Attribution is split across several lines of work.
assessment.maturity: About 15 to 20 years of use. It is influential, but the measurement of misallocation is sensitive to assumptions and has had measurement-error critiques.
uncertainties: Sensitivity to measurement error and model structure.
Absence of Rogerson from the credited names weakens the attribution.
Partial overlap with the 2018 and 2024 growth and development recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of present bias, self-control and reference dependence incorporated psychologically grounded preferences into formal economics. They have applications in saving, health, contracts and policy design, and they extend the behavioural line recognised in 2002 and 2017.
assessment.attribution: Laibson (quasi-hyperbolic discounting in consumption and saving) and Rabin (the formal introduction of psychology and the theory of reference dependence and fairness) are the most prominent. The field has many significant contributors, including Koszegi, O'Donoghue and Loewenstein, so any selection is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The central work is from 1990s to 2000s and has been widely applied. Evidence on field behaviour is mixed in places.
uncertainties: Prior behavioural prizes (Kahneman and Smith, Thaler) reduce the marginal case.
Difficulty of limiting credit to two or three names.
Replication and external-validity debates in behavioural evidence.
